question: Does the complete development-selected BOUNDARY2 allocation policy improve practical W1 whole-game strength against the accepted production baseline at 10+0.1?
admission: All four planned development comparisons are closed. BOUNDARY2 passes correctness, resource and sampled clock gates and scores .6953125, above the frozen .55 development rule. UNSTABLE2 also passes but scores .6015625 with higher CPU expansion and more low-clock responses. Prefer the simpler extension-off complete policy; the descriptive paired difference remains uncertain. Selection rationale and immutable evidence hashes are recorded separately. No parameter or Search changes follow development.

Matched Cp64SpendingUciMain launcher and 200k-node startup warmup. Both flags3407871, ADAPTIVE16, CP64 S6CNU002/eight heads, BT4_Q_LOGIT400_V1 and Hash64. Network SHA2568431626c2fca81e0a1e9ccd5e45ddd8829e6e3282c756c21fad75b06d075bb2b. Existing runtime and calibration bindings remain immutable; no rebuild or production selection change.
policy: Same qualified BOUNDARY2 v1: hard=min(2*original baseline allocation, remaining-50ms), fixed before Search. Nominal=ceil(hard/2); from completed ordinary depth6, stable3 may stop at ceil(nominal/2), otherwise stop at the first completed boundary at/after nominal. No extra iteration for a just-changed move. Hard/node/external limits dominate; mate scores are not numerical stability evidence. Explicit non-clock request modes preserve their semantics.
openings: Select all128 fresh unique paired/color-reversed eight-full-move openings from the locally preserved source book, partition1, before any independent game. Exclude every available tracked historical selection receipt, all current frozen selections (played or unplayed), all current trajectory-history prefixes and the prior CP64/TT development-corpus exclusions. No evaluator/outcome filtering. Freeze the full selection, four consecutive32-pair splits, exact source/selector/exclusion hashes and seeds. No development or historical confirmation game is reused.
samplingAssumptions: Both uncertainty methods assume representative independent opening-pair outcomes in this domain. Neither resolves systematic opening-family, persistent process-state, scheduling or clock effects. Unique held-out openings, color reversal and fresh processes per block mitigate rather than prove absence of bias.

analysis.primary: One final128-pair mean after all four qualified blocks. Each pair is the mean of its two color-reversed game scores. Sample variance uses n-1; standard error=sqrt(variance/n). Two-sided95% normal-approximation interval uses NormalDist.inv_cdf(.975). Positive support requires its lower score bound strictly greater than .5 plus all correctness/resource/clock gates. This is an approximate model-based inference, not an exact finite-sample guarantee.
analysis.sensitivity: Also report bounded-pair Hoeffding95% with radius sqrt(log(40)/(2*128)), W/D/L, pentanomial, pair scores and logistic Elo transforms. If the bounded interval includes .5, explicitly say this conservative sensitivity does not independently establish superiority. Both methods share the sampling/domain assumptions.
analysis.dispositions: Primary lower>.5 is positive under the recorded primary assumptions; primary upper<.5 is negative; otherwise inconclusive. Zero variance yields no normal interval and is inconclusive unless separately identified bounded evidence supports a conclusion. No automatic adoption follows any result.
analysis.multiplicity: Exactly one development-selected complete profile is admitted at alpha .05 on fresh independent data. No second finalist, alternate formulation, outcome-based extension, fallback candidate or transfer of samples after confirmation begins.
analysis.sampleRationale: 128 pairs provides four times the development sample and roughly halves its standard error if pair variance persists. At the observed BOUNDARY2 development variance the approximate95% score half-width is about .049, versus .098 at32 pairs. This informative fixed screen follows existing bounded confirmation infrastructure; no universal minimum game count or gain is asserted. Reassess only after the frozen final look, without extending it.

clockReliability: All games must end normally with legal history and completed-node/whole-request integrity. Audit every per-color clock conservation equation, including initial10100ms; infer original baseline versus reserve-capped doubled candidate hard allocations using the source-verified runner clock. Require maximum request elapsed-over-hard<=25ms in every block. Report actual charges, pre-increment reserves, responses below500ms, soft stops and incomplete work. Development minimum reserve95ms and37 low-clock responses remain visible limitations. Sampled checks are not worst-case scheduling guarantees; preserve any adverse tail or flag.
stopping: No interim score inspection, tuning, statistical futility look, game exclusion or sample extension. Stop the affected confirmation on integrity/correctness/clock/resource failure or owner interruption; preserve all partial/completed evidence. Never replay a started block or substitute an unqualified block. Failed prelaunch admission may retry identical inputs in a fresh attempt at least15min later. Completed qualified blocks may resume only after unchanged evidence verification and with no unclosed block. An incomplete study is operationally inconclusive, not the planned128-pair result.
